name: South End Historic District bowfront rows

dates.note: Wikipedia states 'The area's principal development took place 1850-1873'; the City of Boston says 'development began in 1850 by real estate speculators building fashionable, single-family rowhouses'.

refs.title: South End Historic District - NRHP reference No. 73000324 (original), added May 8, 1973, with boundary increases 14001095 (2014) and 100011759 (2025) (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
refs.note: A DISTRICT listing and not an identity for any one building. Read from the infobox, not from the National Register's own database.

refs.title: South End National Register Historic District Report
refs.note: The report's own words, as the search returned them: 'bow fronted, mansard roofed rowhouses in the Italianate style. The end houses are brought forward to enclose the square.'

refs.title: South End Landmark District | Boston.gov
refs.note: The City's own statement of the mechanism this corpus cares about: 'Restrictions on building size and materials meant residential structures in long uniform rows, resulting in remarkable visual unity'.

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026, WP-11.3 Tranche 2, the mid-nineteenth-century city house cluster. No HABS survey with written historical and descriptive data was resolved for this building from here; the searches that failed are listed in the cluster's report. A record with references and no survey block is complete, and inventing one would be worse than the gap. Carried for one sentence, which is the italianate-townhouse node's central claim written by a city rather than by this corpus: restrictions on building size and materials produced long uniform rows and therefore visual unity. The node says coherence 'was a byproduct of constraint rather than of taste'; Boston's own landmark page says the same thing about the same buildings, independently. Wikipedia also records the district as 'the largest intact Victorian row-house district in the country, covering over 300 acres', which makes it the population the node's argument is actually about.
